reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound: low-temperature annealing of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 to form coherent L12 precipitates is well-supported by prior work on this alloy system, and the proposed strengthening and creep-resistance mechanisms are physically reasonable, though the claim of improved corrosion resistance via precipitate refinement is less directly justified.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with specific measurements and a quantitative falsification criterion (e.g., <20-30% improvement in yield strength), but the test design lacks detail on how cyclic thermal/mechanical loading will be applied and how corrosion improvement will be isolated from other microstructural changes.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis directly addresses the research question by proposing a practical, single-intervention heat treatment to improve strength, creep, and corrosion, making it highly relevant and worth testing for aerospace fastener applications.
